chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fudal narrated to us, from his father, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Thabit ibn Abu Safiyyah, from Sa'd al-Khaffaf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

Allah, the Mighty and High, revealed to David (peace be upon him): 'O David, you will and I will. However, your will is not except what I will. Therefore, if you submit to My Will, I will bestow you with what you will. However, if you do not submit to My Will, I will trouble you in what you wish. In the end, it is always My will that will prevail.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between human will and divine will in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* elucidates the Shia theological distinction between *iradah* (divine will) and *mashi'ah* (human volition), emphasizing that human desires are subordinate to the ultimate divine decree. It highlights the practical spiritual implication that aligning one’s will with God’s leads to fulfillment, while resistance results in tribulation, a concept central to understanding *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters). The text underscores that while humans possess agency in their intentions, the final outcome is strictly governed by God’s sovereign will.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 4. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qittan said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa`id al-Hamdani said: `Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn `Ali ibn Fuddal said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Marwan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Thabit ibn Abu Safiyyah, on the authority of Sa`d ibn al-Khaffaf, on the authority of al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah that The Commander of the Faithful (AS) said:

“Allah, the Mighty and High, revealed to David [Dawud] (AS): O David, you will and I will. However, your will is not except what I will. Therefore, if you submit to My Will, I will bestow you with what you will. However, if you do not submit to My Will, I will trouble you in what you wish. In the end, it is always My will that will prevail.
